name: Dream Theater
reference: 6:00 / Caught in a Web / Lie / Erotomania — Awake (1994); also covers the IIC+-voiced Images and Words (1992: Pull Me Under, Take the Time)
rig: John Petrucci: Ibanez JPM / Music Man-style humbuckers (DiMarzio Steve's Special bridge) -> Mesa/Boogie Mark IIC+ (lead ch, GEQ in a V) AND Mesa Dual Rectifier, rhythms quad-tracked (2x IIC+ L/R + 2x Recto L/R) -> Mesa Rectifier Standard 4x12 V30; rack: TC Electronic 2290 (delay/chorus), Lexicon PCM70 reverb. Images and Words was Mesa TriAxis/2:90 (or Quad preamp, both IIC+-lineage) into Mesa 4x12, JC-120 for cleans
notes: Dual-rig stereo for Awake's quad-tracked wall: left = real Mark IIC+ full rig at classic Petrucci settings (bass 0, mid 8, treble 7.5, all pulls, GEQ V 80/45/20/50/80), right = 90s Dual Rectifier (reissue) Red/Modern full rig into a V30 4x12. Pans are 0.15/0.85 rather than hard, because on the record each amp was tracked both left and right. The IIC+ capture was miked on a Mesa 2x12 V30 (not the 4x12 Recto cab), so it's a little tighter than the record. Images and Words' exact amp (TriAxis/2:90 vs Quad vs IIC+) is disputed; all are IIC+ voicings, so the left rig stands in for it; its lone-IIC+ sound is the left rig alone (not separately switchable). TC 2290 chorus can't be modelled: SW7 spread with light wobble plus a slow align wobble stand in for it. Echo (SW10) = TC 2290-style bright digital lead delay. PCM70 isn't in the catalog: PCM90 (its successor) Rich Plate at a low mix instead. Boost/drive pedals weren't on these records; they're lead pushes (Klon clean lift, TS808 tightener), both off.

left.label: Klon Centaur (silver), low gain: solo volume lift (not on record)
Ibanez TS808, boost setting (gain low, level up): Mark-amp lead push (not on record)
Mesa Mark IIC+ lead: V1 6.35 T7.5 B0 M8, lead drive 6, GEQ V (80/45/20/50/80%), Mesa 2x12 V30, SM57+C414
Lexicon PCM90 INSTR Rich Plate (stands in for PCM70), low mix

right.label: Mesa 90s Dual Rectifier RI, Red ch Modern, Bold, diode (unboosted), V30 4x12, SM57+e906
Lexicon PCM90 INSTR Rich Plate (stands in for PCM70), low mix
